envelope.text: /// type has one layout everywhere; they are not public members here.

why: RESOLVED 2026-10-29 (issue 2114): `rclcpp::ParameterCallbackHandle` is upstream's -- the handle `ParameterEventHandler::add_parameter_callback` returns, with upstream's `SharedPtr` / `WeakPtr` / `ParameterCallbackType` -- now at namespace scope, and the handler's nested `ParameterEventHandler::ParameterCallbackHandle` is an alias of it. The on-set token that held the name (`uint16_t`) is `rclcpp::OnSetParametersCallbackToken` (row `cpp:OnSetParametersCallbackToken`). ENVELOPE: upstream's public `parameter_name` / `node_name` / `callback` members are held behind a pointer instead (as `ParameterEventCallbackHandle` holds its callback), because a public type has ONE layout on every platform (`check-cpp-capability-layout`, RFC-0096 D1) and those members are hosted-only types. So the type exists on a freestanding build too, but nothing there can make one: the handler's constructor is refused there. Test: `parameter_event_handler_runtime.cpp` writes `rclcpp::ParameterCallbackHandle::SharedPtr h = handler->add_parameter_callback(...)` and asserts the nested name is the same type (`just check cpp`). PRIOR ROW: RE-VERDICTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 P3), `declined`/`absent` -> `gap` (issue 2114): the name EXISTS and correlates `same`, so `absent` was false -- found by the new `misdeclared_absences` check. It means something else: upstream's `rclcpp::ParameterCallbackHandle` is the handle `ParameterEventHandler::add_parameter_callback` returns (ours is nested as `ParameterEventHandler::ParameterCallbackHandle` since issue 2024), while our top-level name is the `uint16_t` token `remove_on_set_parameters_callback` takes -- upstream's on-set handle is `OnSetParametersCallbackHandle`. A ported `rclcpp::ParameterCallbackHandle::SharedPtr h = handler->add_parameter_callback(...)` fails to compile on `uint16_t`. PRIOR ROW: the owning handle `ParameterEventHandler::add_parameter_callback` returns; dropping it unregisters. The `/parameter_events` family: every surface PUBLISHES the topic since issue 2023, and the SUBSCRIBING handler is the gap recorded on `cpp:ParameterEventHandler` (issue 2024). This row stays declined because the name means something else on our side: `rclcpp::ParameterCallbackHandle` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/node_parameters.hpp`) is the bounded on-set registration handle, a `uint16_t` slot id rather than an owning shared_ptr, and that is the decline -- not the event handler. Phase 379 W3.
